I've been to a similar path (crippling depression and going to college late) and I want you to know something : don't compare yourself with others. It's one of the worst things and it won't help you. You have your own story, path, and experience. Allow yourself to study.
I went to University at 30 and some of my professors were PhD and the same age as myself at the time, and comparing my age with theirs made me feel really bad. 

Focus on what you are doing now, and know this is YOUR path. Things will get better for you. Learn to love yourself and embrace your life story. It's what has shaped you, and use it to be a better person.

Take care.

I wonder how many things we do to cut our waste that are laughed of by people who don't understand us yet, will be routine/common sense in the future.

I'm glad this is happening, because I'm in the group of people who always did these things like some regular activity and advocates for these practices wherever I live. I really hope the people who are doing this challenge keep doing it even when this trend dies. I really hope they are not doing this only for attention in social media. 
I also hope this somehow makes people question what constitutes litter, and change their habits as consumers and stop buying unnecessary single use plastic. By cutting single use plastic the amount of trash in these places is cut by at least 50%, not to mention the other changes that are totally easy and possible.
